The Terms of Service document is for **Spotify**, a music streaming and multimedia service.

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to your relationship with Spotify and cover the products and services listed on the company's terms page.
* **User Content**: When you submit content to Spotify, such as music or podcast uploads, the company can use it to:
	+ Operate and improve its services. 
	+ Train its AI and machine learning systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Spotify's separate Privacy Policy is linked from the Terms and explains what personal data is collected and how it's used. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You can opt out of this within 30 days of creating a new account. However, Spotify notes that Steam (Valve) has removed mandatory arbitration in 2024, which is an exception.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the Terms. 
* **Contact**: If you have questions about the Terms, you can check Spotify's published legal contact information at [https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/](https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/). 

As for clauses that may be harmful to users, they might want to be aware of the following:

* **Binding arbitration**: This means you'll have to resolve disputes through a private dispute process instead of going to court. While this can be faster and less expensive, some users may prefer the option to take cases to court.
* **Class-action waivers**: In the event of a dispute, you may be giving up the right to join a class action lawsuit with others, which could limit your ability to recover damages. 
* **AI and machine learning data use**: Although the Terms state that user content is used subject to your settings and applicable law, users may still be uncomfortable with Spotify's AI and machine learning training practices.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SPOTIFY TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Spotify and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language for AI-generated playlists/'AI DJ', expanded the User Content license to cover user-uploaded audio/podcasts processed by AI features, and updated arbitration and class-action waiver clauses.

**Service Name:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on our official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to your use of Netflix products and services, including how you interact with us and what you're allowed to do.
* **Content and License:** We use your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train our AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is used and processed according to our published Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Netflix, you must use binding arbitration with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. (Note: This means you can't sue us in court, and you have to resolve disputes privately.)
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** Requiring binding arbitration with a class-action waiver means users are limited in their ability to hold Netflix accountable for harm. This can make it difficult for users to resolve disputes or seek redress.
* **Termination:** The ability for either party to terminate the agreement at any time may leave users uncertain about their access to Netflix services.

**Other notes:**

* Paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members.
* What constitutes a "Netflix Household" is described in clearer language in the updated terms.

Please keep in mind that these Terms of Service are subject to change, and it's always a good idea to review them regularly to stay informed.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

**Service Name:** Disney+ Subscriber Agreement

**Key Provisions:**

The Disney+ Subscriber Agreement is a contract between you (the user) and Disney+ that sets out the rules for using their streaming service. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services offered by Disney+, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content:** Disney+ may show ads on 'no ads' tiers, even if you've paid for an ad-free experience. This change took effect on January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones.
* **Content and License:** Disney+ may use user-submitted content to improve their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Disney+ collects personal data, which is processed in accordance with their published Privacy Policy. You can find out what data they collect and how it's used by reading the policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In the event of a dispute, Disney+ requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court). You may opt out of this process within 30 days of creating a new account. However, it's worth noting that some companies (such as Steam) have removed mandatory arbitration.
* **Termination:** Either party may terminate the agreement, but you'll need to read the live document for the specific conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can find Disney+'s contact information at their published legal page.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* The introduction of ads on 'no ads' tiers may be frustrating for users who've paid for an ad-free experience. This change may make Disney+ feel less valuable to some users.
* The use of user-submitted content to train AI/ML systems raises concerns about data privacy and how it's used.
* The binding arbitration clause may be unfair to users, as it requires them to resolve disputes outside of the courtroom. This can be a drawback, especially if you're dealing with a large company like Disney+.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

**PayPal User Agreement**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services offered on the company's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to all users and encompass various products and services offered by PayPal.
* **Content and License**: PayPal may use user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The Terms reference PayPal's published Privacy Policy, which describes the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most cases require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but Steam is an exception.
* **Termination**: Either party may terminate the agreement according to the conditions described in the document.
* **Contact**: For questions, see PayPal's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* The requirement for **binding arbitration with class-action waivers** may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit against PayPal. This can make it more difficult for affected users to seek collective compensation for unfair practices.
* The **30-day opt-out window for new accounts** may not be sufficient for users to make an informed decision about binding arbitration.
* **Termination** can be initiated by either party, which may result in the loss of access to PayPal services and funds.

Please note that these Terms of Service aim to provide a summary of the key provisions. If you have specific questions or concerns, it's essential to review the full document.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Service Overview:**

These are the Terms of Service for the eBay User Agreement, which govern your relationship with eBay.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services described on eBay's official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: eBay can use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, following your settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy**: eBay's Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed. You're directed to their published policy for more information.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with no class-action suits allowed. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
5. **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specified conditions.
6. **Contact**: For questions about these terms, see eBay's published legal contact information.

**Red Flags:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration**: If you have a dispute with eBay, it'll be resolved through binding arbitration, which may limit your chances of seeking compensation or joining a class-action lawsuit. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Data Usage**: eBay may use your submitted content and personal data to train its AI/ML systems, which might be concerning from a data protection perspective. You should review eBay's Privacy Policy to understand how your data is collected and processed.
* **Termination**: eBay may terminate the agreement, which could affect your access to their services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

**Service Name:** Amazon Conditions of Use

**Key Provisions:**

* **Relationship with Amazon:** These terms govern your relationship with Amazon and apply to products and services mentioned on their official terms page.
* **User-Submitted Content:** Amazon uses your content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. (Note: this means Amazon may use your data to improve its AI features, such as Alexa and Rufus.)
* **Privacy:** The terms reference Amazon's Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes require binding arbitration with a 30-day opt-out window (you can choose not to use this process, but it's required for new accounts). This means you'll have to resolve disputes with Amazon through a private process instead of going to court.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but you'll need to follow the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, check Amazon's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that May Be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** Requiring disputes to be resolved through binding arbitration means you'll have to use a private process instead of going to court. While there's a 30-day opt-out window, this may still be a disadvantage if you're not familiar with arbitration.
* **Limited Options for Dispute Resolution:** By requiring binding arbitration, Amazon limits your options for resolving disputes.

**Additional Notes:**

* Amazon uses AI and ML systems to process your data, which may be subject to change or modification.
* The terms reference Amazon's AI features, such as Alexa and Rufus, but don't provide much detail about how they're used or how you can opt out of their use.

Overall, these terms are fairly standard for a company like Amazon, but it's essential to be aware of the dispute resolution process and how your user-submitted content is used to support its AI/ML systems.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: May 2024 update revised disputes/arbitration to explicitly permit small-claims-court actions, updated language about Amazon services covered, and added clearer references to AI features (Alexa, Rufus) and how generated content interacts with the user agreement.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Amazon to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 .

**Service Name:**
Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions (2024)

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms govern your relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services listed on Apple's official terms page.
* Apple uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* Apple's Privacy Policy sets out the personal data collected and how it's processed.
* Binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is required to resolve disputes, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Flagged Clauses:**
* **Binding Arbitration with Class-Action Waiver**: This means that if you have a dispute with Apple, you'll have to resolve it through private arbitration instead of going to court. Additionally, you'll give up your right to participate in a class-action lawsuit. This clause may be harmful to users as it can limit their ability to seek compensation in cases where many users are affected.

Other important notes:
* Apple can terminate the agreement with or without cause, subject to conditions described in the live document.
* Your submitted content is subject to the terms, and Apple may use it to improve its services.

It's essential to understand that these terms are in place to protect Apple's interests and may not necessarily prioritize your rights as a user. However, these terms are standard in the tech industry, and it's crucial to familiarize yourself with them to know what you're getting into.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

**Service Name: iCloud Terms and Conditions**

**Summary of Key Provisions:**

These Terms of Service, effective as of 2024, govern your relationship with Apple when using Apple's iCloud services. Here's a summary of key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to Apple's products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content**: Apple uses user-submitted content to operate and improve its services, including training AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The terms reference Apple's published Privacy Policy, which sets out how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users must agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement subject to conditions described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

1. **Mandatory Arbitration and Class-Action Waivers**: You may be required to use private arbitration instead of going to court, and you may be blocked from joining a class-action lawsuit together with other users who have similar complaints.
2. **Loss of Control Over Personal Data**: Apple uses user-submitted content to improve its services, which may include AI/ML training, without explicit user consent.
3. **Termination Without Reason**: Either party can terminate the agreement subject to conditions not disclosed here. This means Apple can suspend or terminate your account without notice or explanation.

To understand more about Apple's data handling practices, you should also review their [published Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/privacy/).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Plain-Language Summary**:

These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you (the user) and Snap (the owner of Snapchat). The key provisions are:

* **What the agreement covers**: These Terms apply to Snapchat and its related services.
* **How your content is used**: You grant Snap the right to use, operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems with your submitted content (unless you've opted out).
* **Data sharing**: Snap collects personal data from you and shares it with you as a parent via the Family Center, if you're under 18.
* **Disputes**: You and Snap agree to binding arbitration, which means you'll use a private process instead of going to court to resolve disputes (you have a 30-day window to opt out).
* **Termination**: Either party can cancel this agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, refer to Snap's published contact information.

**Potential Issues**: Some clauses may be problematic for users:

* **Arbitration** (clause 5): This binding arbitration may be unfair to users, as they give up the right to go to court. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Limited control over content**: These Terms suggest that Snap may use your content without requiring explicit permission (clause 3).
* **Data sharing**: As a parent or under-18 user, your data is shared with Family Center (clause 2 is unclear without additional context).
* **Limited termination options**: While either party can cancel the agreement, the conditions for doing so are not clearly outlined (clause 7).

Keep in mind that these potential issues don't necessarily imply Snap's website or service is malicious; rather, they highlight aspects of the agreement that may be unfavorable to users.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

**Service Name:** These are the Terms of Service for Pinterest, the social media platform.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with Pinterest and apply to Pinterest's products and services.
* **Content and License:** When you share content on Pinterest, you grant the company a license to use it to run the platform and improve its AI/ML systems, subject to your user settings and applicable law. This means Pinterest can use your content for recommendations and safety, but check your user settings to see what you're comfortable with.
* **Privacy:** These terms point to Pinterest's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. You can check the Privacy Policy to see what data Pinterest collects and how it's used.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with Pinterest, you're required to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but check the specific details.
* **Termination:** Either you or Pinterest can terminate the agreement, but check the live document for the conditions that apply.
* **Contact:** If you have questions, you can find Pinterest's published legal contact information on the new Terms of Service URL.

**User Harm-Flagged Clauses:**

* The requirement for binding arbitration may limit your options for resolving disputes and could result in higher costs or less favorable outcomes than going to court.
* The lack of a clear opt-out policy for existing accounts may leave long-time users vulnerable to this arbitration requirement.
* The license granted by users for their content may have unintended consequences, such as increased surveillance or profiling by Pinterest. However, this depends on your individual user settings.

**Notes:**

* The Terms of Service highlight that they've updated the arbitration provisions, which may impact users.
* There's a link to the previous version of the Terms of Service in case you want to review the changes.
* Please note that these Terms of Service do not address some potential concerns, such as user account suspension without notice or requirements for users to pay any costs associated with arbitration.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** These are the Terms of Service for Dropbox, which govern your relationship with the company and apply to its products and services.

**Main Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to most of Dropbox's products and services, but you can check their official terms page for specific details on what's included.
* **Content and License:** When you use Dropbox, you're allowing the company to use your content to operate, improve, and (where applicable) train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems. However, this only happens according to your settings and the law.
* **Privacy:** The terms mention Dropbox's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how they process it.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's a disagreement between you and Dropbox, you'll likely have to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court). There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but this applies only to accounts opened after the new terms went into effect.
* **Termination:** Either you or Dropbox can end the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about the terms, check Dropbox's published legal contact information on their website (https://www.dropbox.com/terms). You can also find their previous version of these terms on the internet archive (https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms).

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Binding arbitration:** As mentioned earlier, this means that you'll have to resolve disputes with Dropbox in private arbitration sessions instead of going to court. This could limit your recourse in case of a dispute.
* **Class-action waivers:** By agreeing to the terms, you're giving up your right to join a class-action lawsuit against Dropbox if there's a widespread issue affecting multiple users.
* **Usage of user content for AI training:** While the terms state that this only happens according to your settings and the law, you should be aware that your content might be used to train AI and ML systems without additional consent.

It's essential to note that these terms are a contract between you and Dropbox, and it's crucial to be aware of the provisions before using their services. If you're unsure about any aspect of the terms, I recommend reviewing the full document carefully or seeking advice from a legal professional if necessary.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Canva Terms of Use

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Canva, the company uses it to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means that Canva can use your content in various ways, including training its AI tools.

This means you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit against Canva. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either Canva or you can terminate the agreement, but the conditions are outlined in the live document (not explicitly stated here).

**Harmful Provisions to Note:**

* **Ownership and Use of User-Generated Content**: When you use Canva's generative AI tools (such as Magic Studio), the outputs you create are owned by Canva subject to platform rights. This means Canva has significant control over the content you create.
* **Restrictions on Using AI-Generated Content**: You're not allowed to use Canva-generated content to train other AI models. This restriction might limit your ability to use the content in other ways or to share it with others.
* **Content-Moderation Labeling Requirements**: There are new requirements for labeling and moderating content, which might lead to stricter content guidelines.
* **Arbitration and Class-Action Waiver**: The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might make it harder for users to resolve disputes and seek justice.

Overall, these Terms of Service aim to clearly define how Canva uses user-submitted content, governs disputes, and provides contact information. However, users should be aware of the provisions that may impact their ownership, use, and control over their content.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

**Service Name:** Notion Terms of Service.

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms explain your relationship with Notion and cover its products and services.
* Content you submit is used by Notion to operate, improve its services, and train its AI/ML systems (subject to your settings and applicable law).
* Notion's Privacy Policy is cross-referenced for more information on the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* Disputes will mostly be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with some exceptions. You have 30 days to opt-out of this arrangement if you create a new account.
* Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions, which are detailed in the live document.

**Clauses that may be potentially harmful to the user:**

* **Content and License:** This provision states that content submitted by the user can be used by Notion for various purposes, including training its AI/ML systems. This could potentially infringe upon a user's copyright or intellectual property rights.
* **DISPUTE RESOLUTION:** The use of binding arbitration might not be favorable for users who prefer to take their disputes to court. This process might also make it harder to join class-action lawsuits.
* **TERMINATION:** Users should carefully review the conditions for terminating the agreement, as it might be challenging to do so in certain situations.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Terms Scope**: These terms govern your relationship with Figma and apply to the company's products and services. 

**Content and License**: You agree to allow Figma to use your submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.

**Key Changes**:
* Figma can train its AI systems with user content if you opt-in.
* Your content won't be used to train third-party models without opt-in.

**Privacy**: The company's Privacy Policy is referenced, which explains how Figma collects personal data.

**Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means users might give up their right to take Figma to court or join a class action lawsuit.

**Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions stated in the live document.

Potential concerns for users:
* Mandatory arbitration might prevent users from taking Figma to court or joining a class action lawsuit.
* Figma is allowed to use user content to train its AI system, which may involve third-party collaboration.
* There is no clear outline as to the specific user content used or for what purpose it is used.

These concerns could be considered "harmful to the user".
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service (2024 version)

The Terms of Service are agreements between you and Stack Overflow that govern your relationship with the company and its services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all products and services described on Stack Overflow's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Stack Overflow, the company uses it to operate, improve, and sometimes train its AI and machine learning systems. The license allows for non-commercial use, but commercial use may require a separate agreement.
* **Privacy:** The terms refer to Stack Overflow's separate Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. You can find the Privacy Policy elsewhere on the website.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's a conflict, Stack Overflow requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with certain restrictions (class-action waivers, but with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts). Note that not all cases are subject to this requirement.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions specified in the document.
* **Contact:** To ask questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information on the website.

As for potentially **harmful clauses for the user:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The binding arbitration requirement may limit your access to court and potentially make it harder to join a class-action lawsuit.
* **Generative AI / LLM Restriction:** Although this clause explicitly licenses user-submitted content under CC BY-SA, it restricts bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, which might limit how users can reuse their own content for non-commercial purposes.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

The Terms of Service are for Quora, a platform for users to ask and answer questions.

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Relationship with Quora**: These Terms govern your relationship with Quora and apply to the various products and services offered by the company, as detailed on Quora's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Quora uses your user-submitted content (e.g., answers, comments) to operate, improve, and train its AI and Machine Learning (ML) systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Quora's Privacy Policy explains how the company collects and processes personal data. You should review the Privacy Policy for more information.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you may give up the right to sue Quora in court.
* **Termination**: Either Quora or you can terminate the agreement, but the live document will describe the specific conditions.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these Terms, please refer to Quora's published legal contact information.

As for clauses that may be potentially harmful to users:

* **Binding Arbitration**: As mentioned, this may limit your right to sue Quora in court. However, there is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

Please note that these Terms seem to be focused on how Quora will use user data to improve its services, including AI and ML systems. If you're concerned about any specific provision, I recommend reviewing the Terms carefully and reading the Privacy Policy.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with 23andMe, a personal genomics company. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to any product or service offered by 23andMe, as described on their official terms page.
* **User Content:** If you submit content to 23andMe, it may be used to improve and train their AI/ML systems, depending on your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** 23andMe's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. (The Privacy Policy is not reproduced in the Terms, but referenced instead.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of a dispute, you and 23andMe will use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with some exceptions. This means you may not have the option to go to court if there's a problem.
	+ If you have a new account, you can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days.
	+ Additionally, some clauses limit your class-action rights, making it harder to join a group lawsuit.
* **Data Breaches:** In the event of a data breach, 23andMe requires users who don't explicitly opt out to use binding arbitration, which may limit their options.

**Clauses that may be Harmful to the User:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** This clause requires users to use binding arbitration for disputes related to data breaches within a 30-day opt-out window. Some users may not find arbitration suitable for resolving disputes.
* **Limited Class-Action Rights:** This clause limits your ability to join a group lawsuit, which may reduce your chances of resolving disputes collectively.

**Termination and Support:**

* Either party can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
* For questions or concerns, 23andMe provides contact information and a link to their published Privacy Policy.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Service Name**: Twitch Terms of Service

**Key Provisions**:

1. **Scope**: These terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to products and services listed on Twitch's official terms page.
 * They don't specifically mention which products and services are covered.
2. **User Content License**:
 * Twitch uses user-submitted content (like videos, clips, and images) to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems.
 * This use happens subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
 * A key point here is that the terms expand the license to cover clips, replays, and AI-generated highlights.
3. **Dispute Resolution**:
 * Binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is required; if you disagree with Twitch, you'll use this process.
 * Most users must opt out of arbitration within 30 days of creating their new account; a notable exception is Steam (Valve).
4. **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under conditions described in the live document.
5. **Contact**: For questions, see Twitch's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL.

**Potential Risks to the User**:

* **Binding Arbitration**: Requiring arbitration instead of the regular court system can limit the user's rights and be less favorable.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: Arbitration rules may include class-action waivers, which prevent collective lawsuits and further restrict the user's options.
* **Limited Options for Termination**: The terms don't specify the conditions for termination, making it unclear when the user can end their agreement with Twitch.
* **Lack of Transparency about Covered Products/Services**: The terms don't provide detailed information on which specific products and services are governed by these rules.

These are potential issues and are not conclusive. The Terms of Service don't specifically prohibit or restrict users' actions. It's essential to review the terms carefully and consult additional resources for further clarification.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

**Service Name:** Roblox Terms of Use

**Summary:** The Roblox Terms of Use outline the agreement between you (the user) and Roblox when you use their products and services. The key provisions are:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Roblox products and services, which are listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Roblox, they can use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms refer to Roblox's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Service Name:** Steam Subscriber Agreement (between you and Steam/Valve)

**Summary:** The Steam Subscriber Agreement outlines the terms of use for the Steam service, which includes accessing and enjoying various games and features offered by Steam. This document acts as a contract between you and Steam, governing how you can use their services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **1. Scope:** The agreement applies to all products and services described on Steam's official terms page.
* **2. Content and License:** When you submit content, Steam may use it to improve their systems, like AI/ML, but this is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **3. Privacy:** The agreement cross-references Steam's published Privacy Policy, which details the types of personal data collected and processed.
* **5. Dispute Resolution:** For most users, this means binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, note that Steam (Valve) has removed mandatory arbitration.
* **6. Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement based on conditions described in the live document.
* **7. Contact:** If you have questions about the terms, look for published legal contact information on Steam's website.

**Harmful or Worrisome Clauses:**

* **Disclaimer (missing):** There is no explicit warning about the consequences of using Steam services, but it's essential to be aware that using Steam's service implies acceptance of these terms.
* **Mandatory Arbitration (formerly):** Although Steam removed this clause, it might still be present in other areas of their services. This means, in cases where the clause was present, you may have agreed to resolve disputes outside of court.
* **Limitations to Dispute Resolution:** For most users, arbitration with a class-action waiver means you may be limited in your ability to participate in a class action lawsuit, which can be a significant concern when it comes to larger issues affecting multiple users.
* **Changes to User-Generated Content:** Even though the agreement aims to be subject to your settings and applicable law, be aware that user-submitted content can still be used for AI/ML purposes.

It's essential to note that while these terms are in place, using Steam's services still requires you to agree to their terms. It's a good idea to carefully review the agreement and consider opting out of arbitration if possible, especially if you're concerned about the clauses mentioned above.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

The Terms of Service apply to Epic Games' products and services, which are described on the company's official terms page.

Let's break down the key provisions:

**1. What They Cover:** These Terms of Service govern the relationship between you and Epic Games when using their products and services.

**2. Changes and Updates:** Epic Games updates these Terms regularly, and the latest update in 2024 made changes, including:

* New rules for user-generated content (e.g., what happens to the content after you create it)
* Creator-payout rules (i.e., how Epic Games pays the creators of user-generated content)
* EU-specific consumer rights (concerning the Distance Marketing Act)
* Refreshed dispute-resolution sections

**3. Content and License:**

* When you submit content (e.g., images, videos, text) to Epic Games, you're granting them permission to use, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (as allowed by your settings and applicable law).
* This includes using your content to create new AI/ML models.

**4. Privacy and Data Collection:**

* Epic Games will handle your personal data according to their published Privacy Policy.
* The Privacy Policy explains the types of personal data they collect and how it's processed (e.g., sharing it with third parties or using it for marketing).

**5. Dispute Resolution:**

* Most Users will be required to go through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court) with **class-action waivers** (you can't join a group lawsuit).
* There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts; however, some services (like Steam) may have different terms regarding arbitration.
*

**6. Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specified conditions described in the live document.

Key clauses that may be **harmful to the user**:

* **Binding arbitration and class-action waivers** (mentioned in section 5) might make it difficult for users to participate in collective lawsuits or have their disputes resolved by a judge.
* **Granting permission for user content** (section 3) might raise concerns about the types of uses Epic Games can make of your content (e.g., training AI/ML systems, sharing with third parties).

Please note that these are concerns based on the provided text, and it's always a good idea to carefully review the Terms of Service yourself or seek legal advice if you have unclear questions or specific concerns.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Service Name:** DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service

These Terms of Service (or "TOS") govern your relationship with DoorDash, a food delivery and ordering service. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These TOS apply to DoorDash's products and services, including any changes or updates made to them.

**Content and License**: When you submit content, such as ratings or reviews, DoorDash may use it to improve their services or train their AI/ML systems. However, they will use it in accordance with your settings and applicable laws.

**Privacy**: The TOS doesn't fully disclose how much personal data DoorDash collects, as it cross-references their published Privacy Policy. You can find more information on their data collection and processing there.

**Dispute Resolution**: To resolve disputes, you are usually required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with a class-action waiver. However, you can opt-out of this requirement within 30 days of opening a new account.

**Termination**: Either you or DoorDash can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions listed in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses**:

* **Forced Arbitration**: You may be forced to participate in private arbitration instead of going to court, which can limit your options for resolving disputes.
* **Class-Action Waivers**: You may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit, even if other users have similar complaints.

**Red Flags**:

* The TOS rely on a separate Privacy Policy to disclose data collection and processing information, which may not be easily accessible.
* The arbitration requirement and class-action waiver may limit your options for resolving disputes.
* The TOS may be subject to change, and it's up to you to check for updates.

Overall, it's essential to read and understand these TOS before using DoorDash's services to know what you're agreeing to. If you have concerns about these provisions, you may want to consider alternative services.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you (the user) and Uber regarding the use of Uber's products and services. The latest version (2024) includes changes affecting arbitration, AI-generated trip summaries, and third-party services liability.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The terms govern your relationship with Uber and apply to all Uber products and services.
* **Content and License:** Uber can use your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. (Note: This means Uber can use your content, but it's also bound by your settings and the law.)

* **Dispute Resolution:** You'll typically resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. **Please be aware that class-action lawsuits might not be possible.**
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement, but conditions may apply.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can find Uber's contact information online.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Arbitration:** As mentioned earlier, arbitration can be limiting, especially with a 30-day opt-out window. If you have concerns, review this option carefully before proceeding.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .
